stem: Dev sets a small paper pinwheel on a stick in the school yard. A steady breeze makes the pinwheel turn. He also watches a toy windmill whose wings catch the same breeze.

parts.text: When is the air acting as wind that can move the pinwheel?

options.text: When the air is moving and turns the pinwheel.
When the air is completely still and the pinwheel stays fixed.
Only after the toy windmill turns first to create the breeze.
Never, because a gentle breeze is not wind.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Moving air is wind, and that moving air can turn a pinwheel or windmill wings.

teacher.key_rationale: Wind is moving air. It can turn a pinwheel or windmill. Still air, reversing cause and effect, or denying that a breeze is wind are wrong.
